predecessors.note: The Orašac Assembly of February 1804 elected Karađorđe; Cliopatria's Serbs row starts in 1805.

land.text: Serbia in its 1913 borders with Vojvodina (24-25 November 1918) and Montenegro (absorbed on 28 November 1918); on 1 December 1918 Serbia united with the newly created State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs

successors.note: Infobox of the Kingdom page gives 'Creation of Yugoslavia: 21 December 1918'; its text gives 1 December. Cliopatria's Yugoslavia row starts 1919.

capitals.name: Smederevo
capitals.note: Karađorđe 'proclaimed Smederevo the capital in November 1805'; the infobox also lists Topola without years.

capitals.name: Gornja Crnuća
capitals.note: Infobox 'Gornja Crnuća (1815-1818)'; coordinates approximate (near Gornji Milanovac).

capitals.name: Belgrade
capitals.note: Infobox 'Belgrade (1841-1882)'; 'Capital and largest city: Belgrade' for the kingdom (the Kingdom of Serbia page). The wartime seat of 1914-1915 and the exile of 1915-1918 are not named on the pages opened.

rulers.note: Led the Second Uprising from Takovo in April 1815; infobox '1817-1839 (first)'. 1815-1817 and 1839-1842 are not on the page excerpt.

rulers.name: Mihailo Obrenović III
rulers.note: First reign 1839-1842 (Principality page); Milan Obrenović II reigned a few weeks in 1839 before him. Added by reviewer eu-18-f.

rulers.name: Alexander Karađorđević
rulers.note: Reign began 14 September 1842 ('overthrown by the Defenders of the Constitution').

rulers.name: Milan Obrenović IV (Milan I)
rulers.note: Reign began 10 June 1868; prince to 6 March 1882, then king 'from 6 March 1882 to 6 March 1889' (the Kingdom of Serbia page).

rulers.name: Alexander I
rulers.title: king
rulers.note: 'ruled from 6 March 1889 to 11 June 1903' (the Kingdom of Serbia page).

rulers.name: Peter I
rulers.title: king
rulers.note: 'from 15 June 1903 to 1 December 1918' (the Kingdom of Serbia page).

correction.text: Šumadija and Smederevo, the insurgents' core before the fall of Belgrade in December 1806

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1804-1806: Cliopatria begins in 1805 with the full 42,930 km2 outline, but 'the capture of Belgrade meant the control of the entire Pashalik by December 1806' and Smederevo became the capital in November 1805. Before that the insurgents held only the Šumadija of Karađorđe and Smederevo; the pages give no extent for these years, so this core (an okrug and a 25 km circle) is a reading.

correction.text: unchanged outline, valid 1807-1813 only (the first Pashalik of Belgrade plus the districts around it)

keyframe_review.note: 42,930 km2; no area for the uprising on the pages (Revolutionary Serbia gives none). The outline is accepted for the insurgent state at its extent from the end of 1806 to October 1813 ('Restoration of Ottoman rule: October 1813'); the years 1805-1806 are covered by the 1804 keyframe. Its size is 1.76 times the 24,440 km2 that the Principality page gives for 1815 (within a factor of two). Repair check: the First Serbian Uprising page gives no extent either ('gained control of the entire Pashalik' in December 1806; Janissaries still held Užice in 1804; an offensive at Novi Pazar and one in the Timok Valley are named, not held ground), so the outline stays an unverified reading. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1807..1813 from this entry's own 'valid 1807-1813 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: the principality of 1815-1832 as an area-matched reading of the 24,440 km2 of the infobox: the Pashalik of Belgrade

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1815-1847 outline is 41,371 km2 against the infobox's 24,440 km2 for 1815 (ratio 1.69) but 37,511 km2 for 1834 (ratio 1.10): it shows the post-1833 principality from 1815. The page says only that 'in 1831-1833 it expanded to the east, south, and west'. The correction takes eight modern districts (Belgrade, Šumadija, Pomoravlje, Podunavlje, Kolubara, Mačva, Braničevo, Moravica: 92 cells, about 23,000 km2) as the pre-1833 Pashalik; the match to 24,440 km2 is by area, not from a source that lists districts.

correction.text: the principality after the expansion of 1831-1833 to the east, south and west

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1833-1847: the Cliopatria 1815 outline (41,371 km2) is right for the enlarged principality: the page gives 37,511 km2 for 1834 after 'in 1831-1833 it expanded to the east, south, and west'. The decrees of 1830 and 1833 'expanded the same rights to a larger territory' (Miloš page).
41,277 km2: one cell different from 1815; no page opened places a territorial change in 1848. Unverified: page budget.
41,207 km2: the 1848 outline within one cell. Unverified: page budget.
41,371 km2: back to the 1815 outline. Unverified: page budget.
41,348 km2: one cell different for the single year. Unverified: page budget.

41,371 km2 to 1876; the principality's frontier is unchanged by the pages for 1833-1877; the infobox 'On 18 April 1867 the Ottoman government ordered the Ottoman garrison ... withdrawn from the Belgrade fortress' is a change of control, not of frontier.

41,179 km2 is the pre-1878 outline; the years 1877 only. 'In 1878 ... the Albanian territories of Niš, Prokuple, Kuršumlia, Vranje and Leskovac were given to Serbia'; Cliopatria shows the larger outline only in its Kingdom of Serbia row from 1880 (49,696 km2, 30 cells more), so 1878-1879 are covered by the new keyframe 1878.

correction.text: Serbia with the lands won in 1878: Niš, Prokuplje, Kuršumlija, Vranje, Leskovac

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1878-1884: Serbia after the Treaty of Berlin (13 July 1878); the outline is Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Serbia' 1880 shape (49,696 km2, identical to the Serbs 1885 shape), which covers the 1880-1884 gap of this row. Niš, Pirot, Leskovac and Vranje were taken in the war of December 1877 to February 1878 ('On 31 January they took Vranje').

49,696 km2 for 1885-1910, the 1878 frontier; the Treaty of Bucharest page says Serbia had 48,300 km2 before the Balkan Wars (ratio 1.03). Cliopatria's gap of 1880-1884 is covered by the 1878 keyframe.

90,944 km2: Serbia plus the lands its army held by the end of 1912 (Kosovo, Vardar Macedonia, the Sandžak and the northern Albanian coast, 25 cells of which it left in 1913). The ledger records it as occupation: Kosovo, Vardar Macedonia and the Sandžak until the Treaty of London (May 1913), the Albanian coast until October 1913 (Albania during the Balkan Wars: 'The final withdrawal of Serb personnel from Albania was in October 1913').

88,969 km2 against the Treaty of Bucharest page's 'Serbia increased its territory from 48,300 to 87,780 km2' (ratio 1.01). The Kingdom page says the territory 'increased by 81%' (48,300 x 1.81 = 87,400). The Albanian coast is not in this outline, but Serbian troops stayed there until October 1913; that stretch is occupation in the ledger (counterpart albania).
88,969 km2, the 1913 outline unchanged until the invasion of 1915.
88,969 km2, same outline; 'In 1915 Serbia was occupied by foreign troops after a combined invasion'. Cliopatria ends the row here.

correction.text: Serbia in its 1913 borders under occupation; the government and army abroad

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1916-1917: Cliopatria has no shape for the years of occupation. The state continued: the Serbian Army retreated through Albania and fought on the Salonika front from 1916. The 1915 outline stands as Serbia's land; the occupying states record the hatched occupation. The ledger now records the occupation: Austria-Hungary (October 1915 - November 1918) and Bulgaria (October 1915 - September 1918).

correction.text: Serbia in its 1913 borders plus Vojvodina (Syrmia 24 and Banat, Bačka and Baranja 25 November 1918) and Montenegro (28 November 1918)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1918: liberation in October 1918, Vojvodina joins on 24-25 November, Montenegro absorbed 28 November, union with the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs on 1 December 1918 ('On December 1, 1918, Serbia united with the newly created'). Kingdom page: 'At the end of World War I in 1918 it united with Vojvodina and the Kingdom of Montenegro.' Vojvodina is drawn as modern Vojvodina (about 19,700 km2); the Hungarian and Romanian parts of the Banat and Bačka Serbia claimed in November 1918 are not.

region.text: Šumadija, where the vojvodas rose, and Smederevo

ledger.note: 1804: the Orašac Assembly elects Karađorđe and the Serbs rise against Ottoman rule. 'The Orašac Assembly in February 1804 saw the election of Karađorđe to lead the uprising'; infobox 'Established: 1804'; the First Serbian Uprising dates from 14 February 1804 (Serbian Revolution page). The land is Šumadija; the page gives no boundary.
1805: Karađorđe proclaims Smederevo the capital in November 1805 ('proclaimed Smederevo the capital in November 1805').

region.text: the Pashalik of Belgrade and the districts around it as drawn in Cliopatria's 1805 outline

ledger.note: 1806: Belgrade falls and the insurgents control the whole Pashalik of Belgrade. 'the capture of Belgrade meant the control of the entire Pashalik by December 1806.' The pages give no extent; the region is the Cliopatria outline beyond the core.

1807: Karađorđe proclaims Belgrade the capital on 8 January ('on 8 January 1807 ... proclaimed Belgrade the capital of Serbia'); the Porte 'first officially recognized the state as autonomous in January 1807' and the alliance with Russia followed on 10 July 1807 (Revolutionary Serbia page).

region.text: the whole insurgent state, retaken by the Ottomans

ledger.note: 1813: the Ottomans crush the uprising and retake Belgrade in October. 'The Ottoman army crushed the rebellion in autumn 1813'; infobox 'Restoration of Ottoman rule: October 1813'. Serbia has no territory in 1814 (Cliopatria has no shape).

1815: the state is now the Principality of Serbia, recognised by the Sublime Porte (infobox 'Recognition by the Sublime Porte: 1815'; 'Ottoman authorities acknowledged the state by the 1830 Hatt-i Sharif'); a vassal state of the Ottoman Empire (Hatt-i Sharif of 1830, Serbian Revolution page) until de jure independence on 13 July 1878.

region.text: the Pashalik of Belgrade (area-matched reading of 24,440 km2)

ledger.note: 1815: Miloš Obrenović raises the Second Serbian Uprising at Takovo on 23 April 1815 and wins the Pashalik of Belgrade back; the Porte's recognition is dated 1815 on the Principality page. 'The revolutionary council proclaimed an uprising in Takovo on April 23, 1815, with Miloš Obrenović chosen as the leader'; infobox area 24,440 km2 in 1815.

region.text: the lands added east, south and west of the Pashalik of Belgrade (district names not on the page)

ledger.note: 1833: the principality expands to the east, south and west. 'in 1831-1833 it expanded to the east, south, and west'; area 24,440 km2 (1815) to 37,511 km2 (1834); 'The Sultan's decrees of 1830 and 1833 expanded the same rights to a larger territory' (Miloš page). The page names no district.

region.text: the lands Serbia gained in 1878: Niš, Prokuplje, Kuršumlija, Vranje, Leskovac (and Pirot)

ledger.note: 1877: Serbia declares war again on 14 December and takes Niš, Pirot, Leskovac and Vranje. 'Serbia again declared war against the Ottoman Empire on 14 December' (13 December in the page's second-phase section); the first war of 30 June 1876 ended on 28 February 1877 'on the basis of status quo ante bellum'.

region.text: the lands Serbia gained in 1878: Niš, Prokuplje, Kuršumlija, Vranje, Leskovac (and Pirot)

ledger.note: 1878: the Treaty of Berlin of 13 July 1878 ends the contest; Serbia's war lasted to 5 February (infobox end 3 March 1878).

region.text: the lands Serbia gained in 1878: Niš, Prokuplje, Kuršumlija, Vranje, Leskovac (and Pirot)

ledger.note: 1878: Serbia wins independence and the Niš lands. 'Serbia gained international recognition as an independent state, and its territory expanded'; 'the Albanian territories of Niš, Prokuple, Kuršumlia, Vranje and Leskovac were given to Serbia'; the Congress of Berlin ran 13 June - 13 July 1878.
1882: Serbia becomes a kingdom. 'Proclamation: 6 March 1882' (infobox); Milan I 'ruled from 6 March 1882 to 6 March 1889'. The dynasty remains Obrenović; the colour continues.

region.text: Pirot, the Serbian ground the Bulgarian dossier says was returned in 1886, and Slivnitsa, the battle the pages call decisive (the zone the Bulgarian dossier uses)

ledger.note: 1885: Serbia attacks Bulgaria over the union of Bulgaria with Eastern Rumelia. 'The Serbo-Bulgarian War erupted on November 14, 1885, and lasted until November 28 of the same year'; Serbia 'had failed to capture the Slivnitsa region which it had set out to achieve'. Confidence 2: the page gives the day the war erupted, not the first ground taken, and no battle dates.

region.text: Pirot, the Serbian ground the Bulgarian dossier says was returned in 1886, and Slivnitsa, the battle the pages call decisive (the zone the Bulgarian dossier uses)

ledger.note: 1886: the Treaty of Bucharest ends the Serbo-Bulgarian War with no change of frontier: 'leaving the Serbo-Bulgarian border precisely where it had been prior to the war'; 'The peace treaty was signed on February 19, 1886, in Bucharest.' The fighting itself stopped on 28 November 1885. The Bulgarian dossier (Unification of Bulgaria page) puts the same treaty on 3 March 1886 and holds the contest to it; the two pages give different days for one treaty (an Old/New Style difference would fit, but neither page says so). Same year; the page's own day is used here.

region.text: the land the Serbian army held at the end of 1912 and kept in 1913: Kosovo, Vardar Macedonia and the Sandžak

ledger.note: 1912: the Serbian army overruns Kosovo, Vardar Macedonia and the Sandžak. 'Bulgaria, Serbia and Greece declared war on the Ottomans on 17 October' 1912; the page does not date Kumanovo or Monastir ('Their great victories at Kirkkilise, Lüleburgaz, Kumanovo, and Monastir'), so October marks the declaration, not the first ground taken. The Albanian coast the army also took is a separate occupation pair (counterpart albania), because it ended in October 1913, not at the Treaty of London.

region.text: the Adriatic coast and the northern Albanian lands Serbia held from late 1912 to October 1913 (Durrës, taken 29 November 1912, lies in it)

ledger.note: 1912: the Serbian army takes the Albanian coast. 'The army of the Kingdom of Serbia captured Durrës on 29 November 1912 without any resistance'; by the end of 1912 Serbia 'occupied most of the Albanian-inhabited lands including Albania's Adriatic coast', while the Provisional Government of Albania held only a small part of central Albania (Vlorë and Berat). The page calls it an occupation with an administration at Durrës (Drač County), not an annexation. The region is the Cliopatria difference between the 1912 and 1913 shapes (26 cells, including the Durrës cell). The Kingdom page's 'On November 29, 1913, the Drač County of the Kingdom of Serbia was established' has the day of the Durrës capture with another year; the Albania page's 29 November 1912 is followed.

region.text: the land the Serbian army held at the end of 1912 and kept in 1913: Kosovo, Vardar Macedonia and the Sandžak

ledger.note: 1913: the First Balkan War ends on 30 May 1913 (Treaty of London); Serbia keeps Kosovo, Vardar Macedonia and the eastern half of the Sandžak, and the occupation of these lands becomes annexation (next event). 'The First Balkan War lasted from October 1912 to May 1913.' The withdrawal from Albania is dated apart (October 1913, counterpart albania).

intersect.text: the land the Serbian army held at the end of 1912: Kosovo, Vardar Macedonia, the Sandžak and the northern Albanian coast

region.text: the part of the 1912 conquests that Serbia kept in 1913

ledger.note: 1913: Serbia annexes Kosovo, central Vardar Macedonia and 'the eastern half of the Sanjak of Novi-Pazar'. The Kingdom page: 'Sandžak-Raška, Kosovo Vilayet and Vardar Macedonia were annexed'; the Treaty of Bucharest page: 'Serbia increased its territory from 48,300 to 87,780 km2'. Dated to the Treaty of London (30 May 1913), which the Bucharest treaty 'amended'.

region.text: the Vardar Macedonia lands added by the Treaty of Bucharest, east of the 1912 line

ledger.note: 1913: Bulgaria attacks Serbia and Greece on 16 June 1913 and the Second Balkan War begins ('attacked its former allies, Serbia and Greece, on 16 June 1913', First Balkan War page).

region.text: the Vardar Macedonia lands added by the Treaty of Bucharest, east of the 1912 line

ledger.note: 1913: the Treaty of Bucharest is concluded on 10 August 1913; the frontier follows the Vardar-Struma watershed and 'the upper valley of the Strumica remained in the possession of Bulgaria'.

region.text: the Vardar Macedonia lands added by the Treaty of Bucharest, east of the 1912 line

ledger.note: 1913: Serbia keeps the Vardar Macedonia lands east of its 1912 line. Treaty of Bucharest of 10 August 1913: 'Serbia received central Vardar Macedonia'. The region is the Cliopatria difference between 1912 and 1913, in the east of North Macedonia.

region.text: the Adriatic coast and the northern Albanian lands Serbia held from late 1912 to October 1913 (Durrës, taken 29 November 1912, lies in it)

ledger.note: 1913: Serbia leaves Albania under Great Power pressure. 'The final withdrawal of Serb personnel from Albania was in October 1913.' The Ultimatum of 18 October 1913 page (opened) has Austria-Hungary demand that Serbia 'withdraw its troops from Albania within eight days' and Serbia accept on 20 October, evacuating 'as quickly as possible'; it names only Durrës and central Albania and dates no completion. The First Balkan War page ('the Serbs started withdrawing from northern Albania and the Sandžak' after Great Power pressure) gives no date. This replaces the earlier confidence-1 'loss' to albania (the Serbs only occupied the land).

region.text: Mačva (Šabac), the Kolubara basin (Valjevo) and Belgrade, the ground of the Austro-Hungarian offensives of 1914

ledger.note: 1914: Austria-Hungary invades Serbia. It declared war on 28 July 1914; 'On 12 August, the Austro-Hungarian forces, led by General Oskar Potiorek, launched their first offensive into Serbia' (Cer, ended by the 'decisive defeat of Austro-Hungarian 5th Army on 20 August'); a renewed attack across the Drina came on 7 September (Mačva) and the Valjevo Offensive on 24 October. The page names no district; the zone is my reading of Mačva, Valjevo and Belgrade.

region.text: Mačva (Šabac), the Kolubara basin (Valjevo) and Belgrade, the ground of the Austro-Hungarian offensives of 1914

ledger.note: 1914: the Serbs win the campaign. 'The Serbian Army recaptured Belgrade on 15 December' (infobox: 28 July - 15 December 1914, 'Serbian victory'). Austria-Hungary had taken Belgrade on 2 December (the page's lead; its body says 1 December). The Kolubara counter-offensive is not dated on the page.

minus.text: the Bulgarian zone of 1915-1918: Southern and Eastern Serbia (the Niš, Pirot, Toplica, Jablanica, Pčinja, Zaječar, Bor and Braničevo okrugs), Kosovo without Mitrovica, Vučitrn and Đakovica, and Serbia's share of Macedonia (the Morava and Macedonia Military Inspection Areas)

region.text: Serbia in its 1913 borders west of the Morava Valley, minus the Bulgarian zone: the Military General Governorate of Serbia, with Kosovska Mitrovica, Vučitrn and Đakovica

ledger.note: 1915: the Central Powers invade and Austria-Hungary takes Belgrade. 'On 6 October, the offensive was launched'; 'On 9 October Belgrade was occupied by Austro-Hungarian Third Army'; the campaign (infobox) ran 7 October - 24 November 1915 and the page has Serbia then divided between Austro-Hungarian and Bulgarian occupation zones. The Austro-Hungarian zone became the Military General Governorate of Serbia on 1 January 1916 (Austro-Hungarian occupation page: 'Territory of the Kingdom of Serbia west of the Morava Valley'; the zone 'stretched from the region west of the Morava Valley to the Macedonian frontier'); the demarcation line with Bulgaria was agreed on 1 April 1916. Drawn as the 1913 outline minus the Bulgarian zone. Germany's 'control zone' east of the Velika Morava is not drawn (see the notes).

region.text: the Bulgarian zone of 1915-1918: Southern and Eastern Serbia (the Niš, Pirot, Toplica, Jablanica, Pčinja, Zaječar, Bor and Braničevo okrugs), Kosovo without Mitrovica, Vučitrn and Đakovica, and Serbia's share of Macedonia (the Morava and Macedonia Military Inspection Areas)

ledger.note: 1915: Bulgaria occupies southern and eastern Serbia and Macedonia. 'On 14 October, the Bulgarian armies moved into Serbian territory'; infobox 'Date: 17 November 1915-29 September 1918'; 'The Bulgarian occupation zone extended from modern-day Southern and Eastern Serbia, Kosovo and North Macedonia', in two Military Inspection Areas, Morava (command in Niš) and Macedonia (centre Skopje). October is the date of entry, as in the Bulgarian dossier's own occupation_start for counterpart serbs (same months). Its zone is narrower than the one drawn here (Nišava, Pirot, Zaječar, Priština only): the page says 'Southern and Eastern Serbia, Kosovo and North Macedonia' and names Leskovac and Prizren, Gnjilane, Uroševac and Orahovac too; the okrugs are my reading. The Serbian campaign (1915) page has Kosovo divided between two Austro-Hungarian zones and the Bulgarian region, and the Austro-Hungarian occupation page names Kosovska Mitrovica, Vučitrn and Đakovica for the Austro-Hungarian governorate (a planned arrangement), so those three municipalities are left out.

region.text: the Bulgarian zone of 1915-1918: Southern and Eastern Serbia (the Niš, Pirot, Toplica, Jablanica, Pčinja, Zaječar, Bor and Braničevo okrugs), Kosovo without Mitrovica, Vučitrn and Đakovica, and Serbia's share of Macedonia (the Morava and Macedonia Military Inspection Areas)

ledger.note: 1918: the Bulgarian occupation ends. 'The occupation ended in late September 1918, after the Allied offensive at Dobro Polje'; Bulgaria capitulated 'on 30 September' (infobox end 29 September 1918). The page gives no liberation date for Niš or Skopje.

minus.text: the Bulgarian zone of 1915-1918: Southern and Eastern Serbia (the Niš, Pirot, Toplica, Jablanica, Pčinja, Zaječar, Bor and Braničevo okrugs), Kosovo without Mitrovica, Vučitrn and Đakovica, and Serbia's share of Macedonia (the Morava and Macedonia Military Inspection Areas)

region.text: Serbia in its 1913 borders west of the Morava Valley, minus the Bulgarian zone: the Military General Governorate of Serbia, with Kosovska Mitrovica, Vučitrn and Đakovica

ledger.note: 1918: the Austro-Hungarian occupation ends. 'On 29 October, Governor-General von Rhemen and his staff left occupied Serbia'; 'The following day, Belgrade was liberated by the Royal Serbian Army' (30 October); 'By 1 November, all of pre-war Serbia had been liberated' (infobox: 1 January 1916 - 1 November 1918).

region.text: Syrmia (Srem), drawn as the Serbian okrug of Srem

ledger.note: 24 November 1918: Syrmia joins Serbia. 'On 24 November 1918, the Assembly of Syrmia' proclaimed 'the unification of Serb-populated parts of Syrmia with the Kingdom of Serbia'. Before that Syrmia lay in Croatia-Slavonia in the Kingdom of Hungary; 'On 29 October 1918, Syrmia became a part of the newly independent State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs', and 'From 1 December 1918, all of Syrmia was made a part of the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats, and Slovenes'. The Kingdom of Serbia page: 'it united with Vojvodina'. Counterpart austria-hungary is the state that held the land to October 1918; the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs, which held it for four weeks, has no dossier. The Croatian part of Syrmia (Vukovar-Srijem) is not drawn.

region.text: Banat, Bačka and Baranja, drawn as the Banat and Bačka okrugs of modern Serbia (modern Vojvodina minus Syrmia)

ledger.note: 25 November 1918: Banat, Bačka and Baranja join Serbia. The Great National Assembly in Novi Sad 'declared the accession of these regions to the Kingdom of Serbia' ('We join the Kingdom of Serbia'); the regions 'seceded ... from Hungary' out of the 'already collapsed Austria-Hungary'. The Annexation of Vojvodina page (opened): the lands largely matched five counties of the Kingdom of Hungary; the Serbian army entered Novi Sad on 9 November, took Subotica on 13, Pécs on 14 and Timișoara on 15 November; the Allies decided to partition the Banat in June 1919 and Trianon (June 1920) left Yugoslavia a third of it. Only the part now in Serbia is drawn; the Hungarian and Romanian parts Serbia held briefly are not.

region.text: the Kingdom of Montenegro

ledger.note: 1918: Serbia absorbs the Kingdom of Montenegro on 28 November ('On November 28, 1918, it absorbed the Kingdom of Montenegro').

region.text: Serbia in its 1913 borders with Vojvodina and Montenegro

ledger.note: 1918: on 1 December Serbia unites with the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs, the new Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes. 'On December 1, 1918, Serbia united with the newly created' state; the infobox gives 21 December 1918 for the creation of Yugoslavia. The land handed on includes Vojvodina (joined 24-25 November 1918) and Montenegro (28 November 1918).

wars.name: First Serbian Uprising
wars.outcome: The insurgents took the whole Pashalik of Belgrade by December 1806; the Porte recognised the state as autonomous in January 1807; Russia allied with Serbia on 10 July 1807; the Treaty of Bucharest of May 1812 dealt with the Serbs in Article 8; the Ottomans retook Belgrade in October 1813.
wars.note: 'First Serbian Uprising: 14 February 1804 - 7 October 1813' (Serbian Revolution page).

wars.name: Second Serbian Uprising
wars.outcome: Proclaimed at Takovo on 23 April 1815; in mid-1815 Miloš Obrenović negotiated with the Ottoman governor Marashli Ali Pasha; the Porte recognised the principality in 1815. The fighting changed no frontier beyond the restoration of the Pashalik.

wars.name: Serbian-Ottoman War (1876-1877)
wars.outcome: Serbia declared war on 30 June 1876; 'Peace was signed on 28 February 1877 on the basis of status quo ante bellum'.

wars.name: Serbian-Ottoman War (1877-1878)

zones.text: the lands Serbia gained in 1878: Niš, Prokuplje, Kuršumlija, Vranje, Leskovac (and Pirot)

wars.outcome: Serbia took Niš, Pirot, Leskovac and Vranje (Vranje on 31 January 1878); the Treaty of Berlin of 13 July 1878 gave Serbia independence and Niš, Prokuplje, Kuršumlija, Vranje and Leskovac.
wars.note: Phase two ran 13 December 1877 - 5 February 1878; the infobox ends the wars on 3 March 1878.

wars.name: Serbo-Bulgarian War

zones.text: Pirot, the Serbian ground the Bulgarian dossier says was returned in 1886, and Slivnitsa, the battle the pages call decisive (the zone the Bulgarian dossier uses)

wars.outcome: Serbia declared war over the union of Bulgaria and Eastern Rumelia and attacked on 14 November 1885; it 'had failed to capture the Slivnitsa region which it had set out to achieve' and the fighting stopped on 28 November 1885; the Treaty of Bucharest (19 February 1886 on this page) left 'the Serbo-Bulgarian border precisely where it had been prior to the war'. No border change.
wars.note: 'The Serbo-Bulgarian War erupted on November 14, 1885, and lasted until November 28 of the same year.' The Bulgarian dossier has the mirror contest pair (November 1885 - March 1886).

wars.name: First Balkan War

zones.text: the land the Serbian army held at the end of 1912: Kosovo, Vardar Macedonia, the Sandžak and the northern Albanian coast

wars.outcome: The Balkan League overran Ottoman Europe; Serbia held Kosovo, Vardar Macedonia, the Sandžak and the northern Albanian coast and withdrew from Albania under pressure from the Great Powers; the war ended 30 May 1913 (Treaty of London).

wars.name: Second Balkan War

zones.text: the Vardar Macedonia lands added by the Treaty of Bucharest, east of the 1912 line

wars.outcome: Bulgaria attacked Serbia and Greece on 16 June 1913 and lost; the Treaty of Bucharest of 10 August 1913 gave Serbia central Vardar Macedonia and Kosovo and 'the eastern half of the Sanjak of Novi-Pazar'.
wars.note: The Kingdom of Serbia page lists Serbia, Greece, Romania, the Ottoman Empire and Montenegro as fighting Bulgaria.

wars.name: Serbian campaign (World War I)
wars.outcome: 1914: Austria-Hungary invaded in August (first offensive 12 August; Cer, 'decisive defeat of Austro-Hungarian 5th Army on 20 August'), took Belgrade on 2 December and lost it on 15 December ('Serbian victory'; 28 July - 15 December 1914). 1915: Germany, Austria-Hungary and Bulgaria overran Serbia between 7 October and 24 November 1915 (Belgrade 9 October, Bulgaria declared war 14 October, Skopje 22 October, Mitrovica and Pristina 23 November); the 135,000 soldiers of the Serbian Army retreated through Albania. 1916-1918: the Military General Governorate of Serbia (1 January 1916 - 1 November 1918) and the Bulgarian zone (17 November 1915 - 29 September 1918) held the country until the Allied offensive: Bulgaria capitulated on 30 September, Belgrade was liberated on 30 October, all of pre-war Serbia by 1 November 1918.
wars.note: Years 1914-1918 from the 1914 campaign page (28 July - 15 December 1914), the 1915 campaign page (7 October - 24 November 1915, 'Central Powers victory; Serbian retreat through Albania') and the Austro-Hungarian and Bulgarian occupation pages. Fighting on Serbian soil began in 1914, not 1915. Contest pair for 1914 (counterpart austria-hungary) and the occupation pairs of 1915-1918 are in the ledger.

certainty.note: The frontier of the insurgent Pashalik and of the vassal principality is not given as a line by any page opened; the decrees of 1830 and 1833 enlarged it without naming districts.
Fixed by the Treaty of Berlin (13 July 1878); the line itself is Cliopatria's outline, not a page.
The Albanian, Macedonian and Sandžak lands are a wartime occupation line.
Fixed by the Treaty of Bucharest of 10 August 1913 (and the Treaty of London of 30 May 1913).
Serbia is under occupation; the 1913 outline stands for its claim.

sources.title: Revolutionary Serbia
sources.note: 1804-1813 dates, Orašac Assembly, Smederevo (Nov 1805), Belgrade and the Pashalik (Dec 1806), 1807 recognition, 1813; no area.

sources.title: Principality of Serbia
sources.note: Infobox areas 24,440 km2 (1815) and 37,511 km2 (1834), capitals, rulers, 1830, 1831-1833 expansion, 1867, 1878, 1882.

sources.title: Serbian Revolution
sources.note: 14 February 1804 - 7 October 1813, Belgrade capital 8 January 1807, Takovo 23 April 1815, Hatt-i Sharif 1830.

sources.title: Miloš Obrenović
sources.note: Thin: the decrees of 1830 and 1833 'expanded the same rights to a larger territory'; no district names, no areas. Re-read in the repair: still no district names and no area for 1831-1833.

sources.title: Serbian-Ottoman Wars (1876-1878)
sources.note: War dates, Vranje 31 January 1878, Niš/Prokuplje/Kuršumlija/Vranje/Leskovac to Serbia. Found by a search for the title; two guessed titles failed.

sources.title: Kingdom of Serbia
sources.note: Kingdom 6 March 1882, rulers, Balkan Wars (+81%), 1915, 1916, 28 November and 1 December 1918; no area figures. Re-read for the repair: 14-28 November 1885 war, treaty 19 February 1886, 'united with Vojvodina' (no date), Drač County 'November 29, 1913'.

sources.title: First Balkan War
sources.note: October 1912 - May 1913, 16 June 1913, withdrawal from northern Albania; thin on Serbian battles.

sources.title: Treaty of Bucharest (1913)
sources.note: 10 August 1913, Serbia 48,300 to 87,780 km2, Vardar Macedonia, Kosovo, half the Sanjak.

sources.title: Serbian campaign (1914)
sources.note: Infobox 28 July - 15 December 1914, 12 August first offensive, Cer 20 August, Belgrade 2 December (lead) or 1 December (body), recaptured 15 December; Serbian victory.

sources.title: Serbian campaign (1915)
sources.note: Infobox 7 October - 24 November 1915; offensive 6 October, Belgrade 9 October, Bulgaria declares war 14 October, Skopje 22 October, Mitrovica and Pristina 23 November; Serbia divided into Austro-Hungarian and Bulgarian zones; no German zone.

sources.title: Austro-Hungarian occupation of Serbia
sources.note: Military General Governorate of Serbia 1 January 1916 - 1 November 1918, zone west of the Morava, Bulgarian zone, a German 'control zone' east of the Velika Morava (undated, economic), 1 April 1916 demarcation, 29-30 October 1918 liberation.

sources.title: Bulgarian occupation of Serbia (World War I)
sources.note: Infobox 17 November 1915 - 29 September 1918; entry on 14 October 1915; Morava and Macedonia Military Inspection Areas; Dobro Polje 15 September and capitulation 30 September 1918.

sources.title: Syrmia
sources.note: 24 November 1918 Assembly of Syrmia proclaims unification of the Serb-populated parts with Serbia; State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs 29 October; Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes 1 December 1918.

sources.title: Great National Assembly in Novi Sad
sources.note: 25 November 1918: accession of Banat, Bačka and Baranja to the Kingdom of Serbia; seceded from Hungary / collapsed Austria-Hungary. Thin on Syrmia.

sources.title: Annexation of Vojvodina
sources.note: Banat, Bačka and Baranja largely five counties of the Kingdom of Hungary; the Serbian army's advance 8-15 November 1918; partition of the Banat June 1919 and Trianon June 1920. No Syrmia assembly.

sources.title: Albania during the Balkan Wars
sources.note: Serbian army in Albanian lands from October 1912, Durrës 29 November 1912, an occupation with Drač County; 'The final withdrawal of Serb personnel from Albania was in October 1913.'

sources.title: Ultimatum of 18 October 1913
sources.note: Austria-Hungary demands on 18 October 1913 that Serbia withdraw from Albania within eight days; Serbia accepts on 20 October; names Durrës and central Albania; no completion date.

sources.title: First Serbian Uprising
sources.note: Belgrade taken December 1806, Smederevo fell November 1806, Ottoman reconquest 1813; no area, no extent for 1807-1813.

notes:
Cliopatria row: 'Serbs' (Q127885, the Wikipedia article is the ethnic group) is in fact the Serbian state 1805-1915: Revolutionary Serbia (1804-1813), the Principality of Serbia (1815-1882, Ottoman vassal) and the Kingdom of Serbia (1882-1918). One dossier, with the Ottoman restoration of 1813-1815 as a gap (loss in 1813, gain in 1815); a reviewer may prefer three dossiers. The dossier runs to 1 December 1918 instead of Cliopatria's 1915 and adds keyframes 1916-1918; the 'Kingdom of Serbia' row (1188-1884) also holds a 1880-1884 shape (49,696 km2) that belongs to this state (it is the same outline as Serbs 1885); the kingdom-of-serbia dossier should give it a 'wrong' verdict with a correction naming this dossier, and the 1878 keyframe here borrows it. The Cliopatria row 'Serbia' (Q1311990, 1918) is another entity and was not touched.
Pages that failed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miloš_Obrenović_I, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbian–Ottoman_War_(1876–1878) and /Serbian–Turkish_War_(1876–78) (url_not_found; the right title was found by search). Thin pages: the Revolutionary Serbia, Serbian Revolution and Miloš pages give no extent for the uprising, no district names for 1833, no Kumanovo or Monastir dates; the First Balkan War page gives no Serbian dates and no Treaty of London terms. So: (1) the pre-1833 principality is an area-matched reading (eight modern districts sum to 92 cells, about 23,000 km2, against 24,440 km2); (2) the 1804-1806 core is a reading; (3) 1833 districts unnamed; (4) 1912 events carry the declaration date, not a battle date; (5) the withdrawal from Albania in 1913 was dated by the shape only (confidence 1), and is now dated to October 1913 by the Albania during the Balkan Wars page (repair of 2026-10-31).
Relations that need events in other dossiers: the ottoman-empire dossier should hold vassal_start/vassal_end for Serbia (autonomy January 1807, 1815/1830 principality, full independence 13 July 1878; garrison out of Belgrade 18 April 1867) with counterpart serbs, and the Austro-Hungarian occupation of the Sanjak of Novi Pazar (Treaty of Berlin) with counterpart serbs only if the sanjak is drawn; the occupiers of 1915-1918 (austria-hungary, principality-of-bulgaria) should hold occupation_start/_end with counterpart serbs (the Bulgarian dossier already does; austria-hungary 1915-10 to 1918-11), and austria-hungary a contest pair for 1914-8 to 1914-12 and the loss of Vojvodina in 1918-11. Not on any page opened: the extent of the First Uprising in 1807-1813 (Krajina, Užice, Sjenica), the Serbian-Montenegrin border of 1913, the wartime capital Niš (1914-1915), Bosnian territory joining in 1918 (Vojvodina is now in the ledger).
Gazetteer names needed: Šumadija, Smederevo, Gornja Crnuća, Topola, Takovo, Orašac, Kosovo Vilayet, Sandžak-Raška (Rascia exists), Vardar Macedonia. Region counts: Šumadijski, Grad Beograd and the other okrugs resolve (country spelled 'Serbia'). Repair of 2026-10-31 (reviewer's four blocking findings): (1) occupation pairs for Austria-Hungary and Bulgaria 1915-1918 added; Germany's 'control zone' east of the Velika Morava is on the Austro-Hungarian occupation page but undated, economic ('Germany declined to directly annex any Serbian territory'; the Germans 'took control of all railways, mines, forestry, and agricultural resources') and overlaps the Bulgarian zone east of the Morava, so no german-empire pair was written; (2) Vojvodina added in two gains (Syrmia 24 November, Banat/Bačka/Baranja 25 November 1918), 1918 keyframe, dissolve region and successor land extended; the Syrmia and Novi Sad pages do not name the previous holder beyond Hungary/Austria-Hungary and the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs (29 October 1918), which has no dossier; (3) the confidence-1 loss of northern Albania deleted; a separate occupation pair for the Albanian coast (counterpart albania, 1912-11 to 1913-10) replaces it, and the Ottoman pair now covers only Kosovo, Vardar Macedonia and the Sandžak; (4) the Serbo-Bulgarian War 1885-1886 added with a contest pair; the World War I entry now runs 1914-1918 with a contest pair for 1914. Disagreement kept: the reviewer suggested dating the Albanian withdrawal from the First Balkan War page, which is silent; the Albania during the Balkan Wars page has it (October 1913). Kingdom of Serbia page error: 'November 29, 1913, the Drač County ... was established' (the Albania page has Durrës taken on 29 November 1912). Gazetteer names added by the repair: Slivnitsa (place; also in the Bulgarian dossier), Vojvodina region resolves. Counterparts without a dossier: austria-hungary (eu-20), german-empire (Cliopatria row exists), state-of-slovenes-croats-and-serbs.
